title: Why You Can't Tickle Yourself
description:
Why does a touch you make yourself feel like nothing, while the same touch from someone else makes you fall apart? In a 1998 study, scientists compared touch people made themselves with the same touch applied by a machine. Self-touch felt less ticklish, and the brain's touch area was less active. The researchers suggested the cerebellum predicts the sensation of your own movements and turns it down.

Sources: Blakemore, Wolpert & Frith (1998), 'Central cancellation of self-produced tickle sensation', Nature Neuroscience 1(7):635-640 (doi:10.1038/2870); Blakemore, Wolpert & Frith (1999), NeuroImage. The cerebellum explanation is a hypothesis.
